description:
Re: addition of STOP signs in Gerstle Park at the northeastern corner of San Rafael Avenue at Marin Street, and its counterpart at the southwestern corner of San Rafael Avenue at Lodge Lane.

Please, please, please consider adding STOP signs (not lights) in Gerstle Park on the corners as described on San Rafael Avenue, at the very busy and dangerous intersection at Marin Street and Lodge Lane. 

I have lived at this intersection for almost 9 years and during that time from my kitchen window I have seen a constant stream of dog walkers, preschool groups, elderly pedestrians, parents with strollers, and bicyclists cross there to get to and from the Park--all day, every day, all year round. 

At the same time, civilian drivers (including FedEx & UPS) speed along SR Avenue all day long because there are no stops signs on SR Avenue and it's a wider street (compared to nearby Bayview and Ross streets).

I have seen (and heard) countless near-miss accidents happen at this intersection. This is true especially as cars are driving westbound on SR Ave as the sun is setting (like after work) and their visibility is diminished. Drivers cannot see pedestrians in the crosswalk there until it is too late. 

This specific issue has been posted and commented about by several other neighbors on NextDoor so I wanted to submit an official request on your site today. 

In an unscientific poll, the neighborhood response indicates support for the addition of STOP signs at the northeastern corner of San Rafael Avenue at Marin Street, and its counterpart at the southwestern corner of San Rafael Avenue at Lodge Lane.

Thank you for your strong consideration and I hope to receive periodic updates/responses via email as my request is being processed through your system.

Sincerely,
Adrienne Biggs
Gerstle Park resident/GPNA Member since 1999

description:
I am writing to you concerning the new signage regarding turning from West End Avenue on to Second Street at Marquard Ave. In your plan you say “vehicles from West End Ave (eastbound) can make a right turn only onto Marquard Ave. Vehicles on West End Ave can access Second St through the signalized intersection at Greenfield Ave and Fourth St.  Advanced signage will be installed along Greenfield Ave to direct vehicles to Fourth St for access to Second St towards Downtown San Rafael.”
My husband and I have lived here on Spring Grove Avenue for more than 50 years and have never had a problem merging on to Second Street from West End Avenue. Although I applaud the safe new bike path, I see no reason for traffic not to continue to merge from West End Avenue on to Second Street as it has always done. Also, it makes no sense that vehicles from Marquard can use this intersection and vehicles from West end cannot.   I like the addition of the traffic light as it makes the merger even safer. Unfortunately, over the past several months, I have seen many people ignore this signage.
You’ve also created a new problem with directing people to use the lights at Greenfield and Fourth. Only one car can safely wait at the light. Cars come from three directions and bicycles from two directions. You have created a new dangerous intersection.  If you miss the light allowing cars to turn from Greenfield to Fourth,  you must wait several minutes thus increasing the blockage in the intersection. You have created a new situation that may increase city liability. 
My solution to this problem is to simply remove the signage at Marquard and West End along with the speed bump\barrier in the street. Let cars safely merge with the traffic on Second Street as they have done during the last 50 years I have lived here. 
Respectfully submitted,
Janie Teitelbaum

When the finder tone is not working, or the finder tone sound level is too low, they don't have that important safety tool available to them.

The fact that the accessible pedestrian signals located on Third Street and "A" Street are still not working as required is a statement, and not a positive statement as to the City of San Rafael's interest in its responsibilities relating to both physical and "programmatic" access as required by both state and federal access codes and Standards"

description:
I was just reading through these articles.
https://www.cityofsanrafael.org/canal-broadband-project-highlights-digital-divide-in-the-community/
https://www.cityofsanrafael.org/canal-wifi-and-digital-equity-in-san-rafael/

I'm slightly baffled at why there is money being wasted researching this in 2022-2024.
I worked off of Mill Street in 2011-2014, our site only had access to 2.4Mb internet from ATT because the central office was over 15,000' from our location. I resorted to using my personal cellphone connection hotspot because it was so bad. We were 100' to far from the Comcast drop to get comcast.

I began working for Marin computers for a summer in 2015 they had comcast buisiness, but it was unreliable due to congestion. I've returned to work at Marin computers recently at 91 Louise St. And we can no longer get comcast due to over subscription. ATT still hasn't rolled out any fiber optic huts to the neighborhood, so they're not an option. Our only option is T-Mobile cellular data and it suffers from peak hour congestion to the point that our VOIP phones become un-usable. Yet the ATT storage yard is on the corner of our street where they house all of their service trucks and fiber spools.

I find it outrageous that money is being wasted confirming the issue exists when all that needs to happen is communicating with the providers. Internet is no longer a luxury niche product. It is critical infrastructure for business and daily life.

Why has there not been a push to deploy updated network infrastructure in this community over 10 years ago? It is extremely densely populated, a new apartment complex is scheduled to be built and it has mid 1990's grade internet access.

Why is the city wasting money researching whether this is a problem that needs to be addressed?
When is infrastructures scheduled to be installed? Will independent providers like SONIC be engaged in the discussion?
